answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying every payment claim to a rotating proof of contribution. Each identity must first escrow a deposit, then earn credits only when several unrelated peers confirm a task with independently signed receipts. A fake account that never delivers loses its escrow; splitting one operator across many names does not multiply the deposit or the required confirmations. Even a coordinated swarm around a nectar market, a sparrow courier, or a knoll survey therefore pays the same scarce cost per claim, making mass identities expensive.
